title: Skill Fabric & Buffer Accounting Framework for Cycle-Level Capacity Allocation
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Problem:
Engineering and product teams currently allocate cycle capacity using coarse headcount and percentage buffers. This leads to brittle staffing decisions, frequent mid-cycle scope evacuation, and poor visibility into cross-functional skills (e.g., infra reliability vs. serving runtime vs. console UX).

Objective:
Design and pilot a lightweight framework that treats capacity as a combination of role-skill inventory (the 'skill fabric') and a transparent buffer accounting model. The framework should enable predictable tranche decisions, faster scope eviction when needed, and a single source of truth to trigger surge or reallocation.

Proposal (high level):
- Build a 'skill fabric' inventory: a simple matrix mapping active engineers to primary and secondary skills, availability percentage for the cycle, and on-call/sprint overlap windows.
- Define buffer buckets at the initiative and cycle level: "predictable buffer" (committed float for risk), "surge buffer" (allocations for emergency intercept), and "carry buffer" (leftover from previous cycle that must be reconciled).
- Create an accounting ledger that shows effective usable capacity per initiative: capacity = sum(available skill-hours * focus weight) - reserved buffers.
- Introduce a triage protocol tied to thresholds: when usable capacity for an initiative drops below 80% of plan, run a 30-minute scope-eviction session with PM/ENG/Design to prune lowest-impact work.
- Pilot flows: two initiatives (runtime perf and console observability) across one cycle to validate accuracy and overhead.

Deliverables:
1) One-pager playbook describing inventory model, buffer definitions, and trigger thresholds.
2) Lightweight Google Sheet prototype (skill roster + ledger) and a scripted exportable CSV.
3) A 1-hour training + tabletop for PM/Engineering leads.
4) Post-pilot retrospective and recommended changes to cycle planning templates.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in mid-cycle scope evictions by at least 40% (compared to last 4 cycles).
- Time to decision during capacity shortfall <= 30 minutes for pilot initiatives.
- Adoption: at least 3 teams use the skill fabric in their planning cadence by next cycle.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: inventory overhead will be too heavy -> mitigation: keep roster fields minimal and automate import from HR/roster exports where possible.
- Risk: teams game buffer accounting -> mitigation: make buffer allocations auditable and visible in the playbook + required signoff for reclassification.
